title: Robust patterning works best from a homogeneous starting state

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Robust patterning works best from a homogeneous starting state

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: In the evolved neural cellular automaton, French flag patterning works less well from random initial cell states, suggesting that robust development is optimized when cells start from a homogeneous undifferentiated baseline, as real embryos do.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: The scaling of goals from cellular to anatomical homeostasis: an evolutionary simulation, experiment and analysis

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Pio-Lopez L 2023, The scaling of goals from cellular to anatomical homeostasis: an evolutionary simulation, experiment and analysis › Computational results › The tissue minimizes error for reaching the target morphology

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: It seems to work less well with random initializations, suggesting that robust development is optimized when cells start with a muted, homogeneous ‘baseline’ state, not highly diverse starting states, which is indeed what is observed in real development

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Pio-Lopez L, Bischof J, LaPalme JV, Levin M, “The scaling of goals from cellular to anatomical homeostasis: an evolutionary simulation, experiment and analysis”, Interface focus (2023), doi:10.1098/rsfs.2022.0072; section “Computational results › The tissue minimizes error for reaching the target morphology”. Scope: In silico 2D neural cellular automata evolved for the French flag problem; analogy to embryos

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2023-goals-02: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.78

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The simulation comparison is directly reproducible. The inference that robust development generally is optimized by homogeneous embryonic baselines is broader and only partially testable with current heterogeneous developmental data.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Across many evolved tissues, compare final pattern accuracy under homogeneous and matched random initial states. Public developmental datasets can separately test whether real embryonic starting states are homogeneous enough for the biological analogy.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The evolved networks were trained from homogeneous states, confounding optimization with general robustness.

Real embryos are not literally homogeneous at molecular scales.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
operationalizability: 0.86
discriminating power: 0.7
analysis feasibility: 0.84
data adequacy: 0.58
data existence: 0.9

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The initial-condition contrast is well defined inside the simulator and could be run if a competent genome is in hand. The public code does not include the saved tissues, and the claim also treats the result as what real development does. The simulation contrast is a partial test; the embryological generalization is not resolved by it.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Initialize the same evolved tissues from a homogeneous cell state and from random cell states and compare final French-flag accuracy. A reliable drop under random initialization would support the simulation half; equal accuracy would refute it. Matching that preference to real embryos is a separate, qualitative analogy.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
'Less well' is not given a numeric margin, and the embryo analogy is not a measurement in the model.

The comparison is described for the evolved system, and champion genomes are not deposited.
